title: Introduce soft-outline variant and adaptive hitbox for icon-pill buttons
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: icon-pill and compact icon-only buttons in dense surface contexts are producing higher accidental press rates (support tickets + telemetry) when tooltips animate or when adjacent touch targets are present. Current rigid hitbox and outline treatments cause visual clutter and unexpected focus behavior in team dashboards and mobile web. This ticket introduces a new 'soft-outline' variant (low-contrast outline with subtle inward padding) and an adaptive hitbox algorithm that expands only on pointer-down and contracts when idle. Goals: reduce accidental activations, preserve baseline visual density, ensure accessible keyboard and screen-reader behavior, and provide consistent behavior in RTL and localized layouts.
acceptance_criteria: New 'soft-outline' button variant available in design tokens and token guidelines
Icon-pill components (compact and dense sizes) adopt adaptive hitbox behavior: normal hitbox = visual bounds + 4px, on pointer-down expands to +8px; keyboard focus must still match visual bounds
No visual layout shift when hitbox expands; expansion must be implemented via overlay layer or pointer region without moving surrounding content
RTL mirror correctness: caret/icon alignment and hitbox expansion mirror properly for RTL locales

Accessibility: 4.5:1 contrast for 'soft-outline' border at default sizes must be documented; keyboard focus ring remains present and visible (meets WCAG 2.1 AA), screen reader announces role and label consistently
Unit and visual regression tests added; e2e hotspot test with simulated touch events shows accidental-press rate reduction >= 20% on provided repro fixtures
engineering_notes: Recommended approach: implement expanded pointer region using a hit-test layer above layout (pointer-events only) to avoid layout reflow
CSS suggestion: use ::before overlay for expansion with pointer-events: auto and transform: translateZ(0) to keep GPU compositing

Platform constraints: mobile web browsers have differing hit-test behaviors; include a small JS polyfill for consistent pointer-down expansion timing (~120ms delay to avoid accidental activation on quick taps), fallback to static 8px padding on older browsers
Coordinate with ENG-28321 (Touch telemetry changes) for measurement and telemetry gating
decisions: Chose low-contrast soft outline instead of full ghost to preserve surface separation in dark themes
Adaptive hitbox will expand on pointer-down only (not hover) to avoid JIT hover expansion in pointer-rich desktops
Keyboard focus will not trigger hitbox expansion to preserve expected tab navigation geometry
Contrast threshold for soft-outline will default to WCAG 3.0 recommendation for non-text controls, but we will document token overrides for high-contrast mode
review_comments: PM - Jonas Rivera (2026-03-04): Verify analytics filter for mobile vs desktop accidental activations before rolling out wide; consider gradual rollout behind feature flag
Eng - Priya Nair (2026-03-06): Implementation looks safe but we need a fallback for legacy WebViews; suggest ENG-28999 as dependency
Accessibility - Omar Santiago (2026-03-08): Please add keyboard-only test cases and ensure focus ring color tokens are separate from soft-outline color tokens

implementation_notes: Phase 1 (design tokens): landed token PR with naming and default values; team to review token migration plan
Phase 2 (component): implement hit-test overlay and soft-outline styles in button component library; add feature flag 'softOutlineAdaptiveHitbox' for controlled rollout
Phase 3 (qa & telemetry): e2e tests + telemetry gating for accidental-press metric; A/B test on 10% of mobile sessions
Rollout plan: start in staging -> internal dogfood -> 10% mobile -> 50% -> full. Monitor accidental press, keyboard navigation regressions, and visual snapshots
